title: String functions and cyclotomic Hecke algebras
summary: In this paper we study the Kleshchev multipartitions that label simple modules of certain cyclotomic Hecke algebras with parameters $1$ and $-1$. The $2$-residue statistic divides these multipartitions into blocks. We deduce a bivariate generating function for the blocks using representation theory. We also relate the generating functions of multipartitions in a fixed block to string functions associated by Kac and Peterson to irreducible highest weight modules of a type $A_1^{(1)}$ affine Lie algebra. By considering matrices formed by these generating functions, we reprove some results of Kac--Peterson on string functions using the Macdonald identities of Rosengren--Schlosser. As an application, we obtain new infinite product formulas for these generating functions.

title: Typical representations of admissible type I algebraic supergroups
summary: We study typical representations of an admissible type I algebraic supergroup $G$. We prove that, for a dominant weight $λ$, the induced supermodule $H^0_G(λ)$ is simple if and only if $λ$ is typical and the induced module $H^0_{G_{\mathrm{ev}}}(λ)$ for the even subgroup $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$ is simple. We establish equivalences between typical blocks for $G$ and blocks for $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$, and give a projectivity criterion for Kac modules over every Frobenius kernel. For connected $SpO(2\ell|2)$ over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic, we classify all simple projective supermodules over Frobenius kernels.

title: Whittaker Functionals for Exceptional Representations
summary: In the study of automorphic forms on covering groups, Kazhdan-Patterson gives a formula that determines when the Whittaker functionals of induced representations can be descended to exceptional representations. In this paper, first, following the original approach given by Kazhdan-Patterson and applying the block-compatible 2-cocycle of Banks-Levy-Sepanski, we fill in several details omitted in the original proof. Secondly, we compare the formula of Kazhdan-Patterson with that of McNamara and Gao, which is formulated in a more general setting.

title: Trilinear Forms for ${\rm GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ via conjugacy classes
summary: It is well known that for a finite group \(G\), the number of elements in ${\rm Irr}(G)$ the set of irreducible representations up to isomorphism is the same as the number of elements in ${\rm Conj}(G)$ the set of conjugacy classes in $G$ although there is no natural bijection between these two sets. For $G={\rm GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $\mathbb{F}_q$ is the finite field with $q$ elements, we give a bijection between ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Conj}(G)$, which behaves well with the tensor product of irreducible representations on one side and the product of conjugacy classes on the other. In particular, we relate the dimension of the trilinear forms with the multiplicity of the identity element in the triple product of the corresponding conjugacy classes.

title: Space-filling curves and small-ball probabilities for the Kloosterman process
summary: We construct explicitly a space-filling curve in the support of the limiting Kloosterman process, using the planar partial-sum curve of the Rudin--Shapiro sequence. The qualitative existence statement was previously attributed to J. Bober by Kowalski. The resulting curve is a closed, $1/2$-Hölder continuous loop whose image contains a specified triangle of area $1/128$. Its Fourier coefficients are purely imaginary and satisfy $|\widehat f(h)|\leq(2π|h|)^{-1}$ for $h\ne 0$. We also prove a uniform lower bound for small balls centred at closed $1/2$-Hölder curves with a fixed coefficient bound, of the form $\exp\{-C\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(2/\varepsilon)\}$. Known functional convergence then gives a quantitative lower bound for the limiting proportion of two-parameter Kloosterman paths approximating the constructed loop.

title: Plancherel Decompositions and Distinctions for $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n+1}$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n}$
summary:
Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We determine the Plancherel decompositions of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n+1}(F)$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n}(F)$, where $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})$ denotes the mirabolic subgroup of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$, and study smooth distinction for both spaces. We carry out the local unfolding procedure of arXiv:1203.0039, Section 9.5, constructing unitary isomorphisms with degenerate Whittaker models by successive Fourier transforms. The isomorphism for the even model is already stated there in Example 9.5.17. The resulting Plancherel formulas are direct integrals of normalized parabolic inductions from the tempered duals of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, respectively, with product Whittaker-Plancherel measures. In the odd case, the parameter map agrees with the prediction of arXiv:2409.04677.
  Using closed parabolic orbits and local Rankin-Selberg integrals, we prove that all representations induced from these tempered data are distinguished for the corresponding model. We also prove that essentially square-integrable representations are not distinguished for the odd model, and that supercuspidal representations are not distinguished for the even model. For the even model with $n=1,2$, we construct distinguished square-integrable representations outside the Plancherel support. Thus, the smooth tempered distinguished spectrum can be strictly larger than the corresponding $L^2$-spectrum. For $\mathrm{GL}_5(F)$, however, we prove that an irreducible tempered representation is $\mathrm{Sp}_4(F)$-distinguished if and only if it is induced from tempered representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_3(F)$.

title: A Non-Split Motohashi Formula for Toric Periods over Number Fields
summary: We establish a non-split Motohashi formula for toric Eisenstein periods over an arbitrary number field $F$. For a quadratic extension $E/F$, we compare toric Fourier inversion for a product of two Eisenstein series with the $\mathrm{GL}_2/F$-spectral expansion of its Rankin--Selberg kernel. The kernel regularizes the product in a cone of absolute convergence. Eisenstein corrections and contour residues give the geometric and residual terms in the meromorphically continued identity. Suitable test data give twisted first- and second-moment formulas for the completed $L$-functions of everywhere unramified toric characters. Over general $F$ these provide an adelic counterpart of the moment formulas of Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec that does not use the geometry of Heegner points. In the CM case, we prove the absolute nonvanishing proportion $4.9\times10^{-4}$ for every totally real base field and all sufficiently large CM discriminants, with the threshold depending on the base field and no restriction on the number of ramified primes. We incorporate inverse Euler factors at small ramified primes into the mollifier. Local unit-group tests control the resulting moments and remove the ramified Euler-factor loss.

title: Density Bounds in Hua's Theorem for Prime Squares
comment: 57 pages. A formalization, up to the Siegel-Walfisz and Hua's Theorems, is here: https://github.com/lacey-gatech/Density-Bounds-in-Hua-s-Theorem-for-Prime-Squares
summary: We prove a density version of Hua's theorem in the five-variable case: if $\mathcal P$ is a subset of the primes with relative lower density greater than $0.82$, then every sufficiently large $n\equiv5\pmod{24}$ is a sum of five squares of primes from $\mathcal P$.

title: Galois Groups of Trinomials with Small Coefficients
summary: We calculate the Galois group of $f = x^n + ax^k + b \in \mathbb{Z}\left[ x \right]$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all $1 \leq \left| ab \right| \leq 3$, $n$ sufficiently large and $k$ coprime to $n$. In particular, we prove that the Galois group of $f$ is the maximal one that its factorization type allows. We do it by proving a new sufficient condition for the Galois group of a factor of a trinomial to be symmetric, which perhaps can be used to derive stronger results of this kind in the future.

title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
summary: For $T > 0$ large, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $ζ$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|^β$ on $I_θ := [ - (\log{T})^θ,(\log{T})^θ]$, for every $θ> 0$ and $β> 0$. As $β$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|ζ|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $σ$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $β_{c}(θ) := 2\sqrt{1 + θ}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $β\leq β_{c}(θ)$, and assigns masses $β_{c}(θ)/β$ and $1 - β_{c}(θ)/β$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $β> β_{c}(θ)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.

title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 2: The Case \(n\log n\)
summary: We prove that $(αn\log n)_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for almost every real $α$, solving a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 3, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021]. Our main contribution is a new four-point counting estimate with a fixed power saving over $N^{7/3}$ at tolerance $N^{-1}$, valid on the ranges left after a first-moment and Borel--Cantelli argument. Its proof reduces the counting condition to the required proximity of an implicitly defined real root to an integer; a Fejér kernel majorizes this condition, and multidimensional van der Corput $A$- and $B$-processes supply the saving. A localized Mellin argument then yields the second-moment estimate needed for the metric conclusion.

title: Metric Poissonian Pair Correlation Property Part 1: The Case \(n+\log n\)
summary: We prove that $(α(n+\log n))_{n\ge1}$ has Poissonian pair correlation for Lebesgue almost every real $α$. This solves a Problem posed by Aistleitner, El-Baz and Munsch [Open Problem 2, Geom. Funct. Anal. 2021].

title: Unconditional Bounds for Two, Three and Four Consecutive Moderate Gaps between Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
summary:
We prove unconditional positive-proportion results for consecutive moderate gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function. More precisely, for every fixed \(0<c\leq 1/4\), the lower asymptotic densities, normalized by \(N(T)\), of occurrences of two, three, and four consecutive gaps, each of length at least \(2πc/\log T\), are at least \(0.3450014\ldots\), \(0.1812517\ldots\), and \(0.0175021\ldots\), respectively. Here zeros are ordered by ordinate and counted with multiplicity, and \(N(T)\) denotes the number of nontrivial zeros with ordinates in \((0,T]\).
  This answers unconditionally and quantitatively a question studied by Gonek and Sahay under the Riemann hypothesis and the pair correlation conjecture. In particular, at the time of their work, it was not known unconditionally that even two consecutive moderate gaps occur infinitely often for any fixed \(c>0\). The proof combines Lamzouri's Hilbert-space formulation of the Montgomery--Taylor second-moment method with local spectral estimates for simple critical-line zeros and a cluster-counting argument that accounts for multiple zeros and zeros off the critical line.

title: Improved explicit Burgess-strength bounds for composite moduli
summary: Consider the character sum $S(M,N)=\sum_{n=M+1}^{M+N}χ(n)$ for a non-principal Dirichlet character $χ(n)$ to a (possibly composite) modulus $q$. Burgess proved that $S(M,N)\ll N^{1/2}q^{3/16+\varepsilon}$, for any $\varepsilon>0$. This was made explicit by Jain-Sharma et al., but only for moduli $q\geq \exp(\exp(9.594))\approx 8.03\times 10^{6373}$. We prove a stronger result that holds when $q\geq 1.627\times 10^{19}$.

title: Arithmeticity of critical $L$-values for Hilbert-Siegel modular forms in the left half plane and $s = 1$
summary: For a cuspidal automorphic representation $π_f$ generated by a Hilbert-Siegel modular form $f$ and a Hecke character $μ$ with parallel signature, we show the arithmeticity of critical $L$-values of the standard $L$-function $L^S(s,π_f, μ)$ twisted by $μ$ in the left half plane. As a consequence, we show the arithmeticity at $s=1$ under the assumption that there exists a nonarchimedean place $v$ such that $π_v$ is unramified and $μ_v$ is ramified.

title: Zagier's 2-3-2 formula for multiple Eisenstein series
summary: We prove a multiple Eisenstein series analogue of Zagier's formula for the multiple zeta values $ζ(2,\ldots,2,3,2,\ldots,2)$. The multiple Eisenstein series identity contains correction terms given by derivatives of odd Eisenstein series. Using the Goncharov coproduct and Brown's motivic version of Zagier's formula, we show that the normalized difference has rational Fourier coefficients. We then use the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-structure and a modularity criterion of Yu to prove the identity by induction.

title: Minimal asymptotic \(g\)-adic bases from arbitrary partitions
summary: Let $g>h\ge2$ be integers. For a nonempty set $W\subseteq\N$, let $\mathcal F^*(W)$ denote the set of its finite nonempty subsets. Let $$A_g(W)=\left\{\sum_{f\in F}a_fg^f: 1\leq a_f \leq g-1,F \in \mathcal F^*(W)\right\},$$ and let $\N=W_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. We prove that $A=\bigcup_{i=1}^h A_g(W_i)$ is a minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$ for every such partition.

title: A $\mathrm{GL}_3$ level analog of Selberg's result for $S(t)$
summary: Let $π$ be a spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newform of prime level $N$ and trivial central character, and define $S(t,π)=π^{-1}\arg L(1/2+\textrm{i}t,π)$. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,π)$, we establish an asymptotic formula for each fixed weighted moment of $S(t,π)$ as $N\to\infty$, for fixed $t>0$. Consequently, under the same weights, $S(t,π)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to a centered Gaussian distribution of variance $1/(2π^2)$. The key input is a weighted orthogonality formula derived from the Kuznetsov formula of prime level.

title: Note on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers
Improved $L^p$ maximal estimates for higher-degree Weyl sums
summary: For each integer $k\ge3$, we establish the following estimate for all $1\le p<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$: \[ \left\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{n=1}^N e(nx+n^kt)\right|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb{T})} \ll_{k,p,\varepsilon} N^{\max\{1-1/K_k,\,1-1/p\}+\varepsilon}, \] where $K_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k+1)/2\}$, $e(z)=e^{2πiz}$, and $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For $k\ge5$, this improves our earlier bound \cite{chen-miao-yuan-zhao} for $1\le p<D_k$, where $D_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k-1)\}$, and, together with the corresponding lower bound, extends the sharp range up to $N^\varepsilon$ from $p\ge D_k$ to $p\ge K_k$. The main new ingredient is a mixed minor-arc moment estimate obtained before taking the time supremum. The minor-arc maximal estimate then follows from a smooth reproducing kernel argument, while the major arcs are handled directly by Poisson summation and classical complete exponential-sum estimates. The reduction from suprema to mean values also yields a short and direct proof of improved $L^p$ estimates for maximal operators on Weyl sums with general polynomial phases, strengthening \cite[Theorem 1.1]{baker-chen-shparlinski}.

title: Mahler Method and Vanishing Theorem
summary:
This paper is motivated by the recent work of Adamczewski and Faverjon [5], who established the algebraic independence of values of Mahler functions satisfying linear functional equations. While their work is a landmark result, some proofs are long and complex. The primary aim of this paper is to simplify those proofs and provide new applications.
  In their proofs, a vanishing theorem for polynomials, rather than power series, is sufficient. We give a proof of the vanishing theorem without using Szemerédi's theorem or Corvaja-Zannier's theorem. In the case of a single transformation, we present a refined vanishing theorem, which allows us to simplify the proof of algebraic independence. We also provide an elementary proof of a vanishing theorem for $q_i$-Mahler functions with various $q_i$.
  As an application, we prove the algebraic independence of certain continued fractions, extending previous results by Hančl, Adamczewski, and Bundschuh and Väänänen in which only linear independence and transcendence had been established.

title: More than 8/9 zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple or on the critical line
summary: We prove unconditionally that the lower limiting proportion of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which are simple or lie on the critical line, is greater than $8/9$, with zeros counted with multiplicity.

title: Lifting mod $p^n$ Galois representations
summary: We generalize the results of Fakhruddin-Khare-Patrikis, which lift odd mod $p$ Galois representations to geometric $p$-adic representations, to geometric lifting theorems for mod $p^n$ representations whose mod $p$ reduction is odd.

title: On a series related to the Möbius function
summary: For a natural number $n>1$ let $P^-(n)$ denote its smallest prime divisor. Alladi and Johnson proved that $\sum_{P^{-}(n)\equiv l \Mod{k}} \frac{μ(n)ω(n)}{n} = 0$ for $(l,k)=1$, and Tenenbaum showed that the partial sums of this series up to $X$ are $O_\varepsilon\bigl((\log\log X)^{5/3+\varepsilon}/\log X\bigr)$. In this article, we prove that these partial sums are in fact equal to $C(k,l)/\log X + O\bigl((\log\log X)^4/(\log X)^2\bigr)$, with an explicit constant $C(k,l)$. We also investigate the behaviour of these constants. In particular, we show under GRH that the number of reduced classes $l\Mod{k}$ for which $C(k,l)<0$ is $\varphi(k)(1- o(1))$ as $k\to\infty$.

title: Fourier dimension for exactly approximable matrices
summary: We determine the Fourier dimension of exactly approximation set for all dimensions. More precisely, let $m,n\ge1$, $\boldsymbolθ\in\mathbb R^m$, and $ψ:\mathbb N\to \mathbb R^+$ be a non-increasing approximate function. Denote by $\textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(ψ,\boldsymbolθ)$ the set of $m\times n$ matrices which are inhomogeneously $ψ$-approximable with shift $\boldsymbolθ$, but not $cψ$-approximable for any fixed $0<c<1$. We prove that $$\dim_{\text{F}} \textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(ψ,\boldsymbolθ)=\frac{2n}{1+τ_ψ},\ \text{whenever }τ_ψ>\frac{n}{m},$$ where $τ_ψ$ is the lower order of $ψ$ at infinity.

title: Cuspidal Class Number Formulae for Intermediate Modular Curves of Prime Level
summary: Let $X$ be a modular curve lying between $X_{0}(p)$ and $X_{1}(p)$, where $p \ge 13$ is prime. The cuspidal group of $X$ is the subgroup of its Jacobian generated by the equivalence classes of differences of cusps. In this paper, we give explicit formulae for the order of the cuspidal group, and two subgroups of it defined over the rationals.

title: Confluence relations, Hoffman basis over \mathbb{Z}_{(2)}, and the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
summary: We express every admissible word as a $\mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$-linear combination of Hoffman words and explicit confluence relations. This implies that every multiple zeta value is a linear combination of elements of the Hoffman basis with coefficients having odd denominators, as conjectured by Hirose and Sato. Combined with Brown's theorem and Furusho's characterization of the Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\mathrm{GRT}$ by confluence relations, our result identifies the de Rham motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives over $\mathbb{Z}$ with $\mathrm{GRT}$ and gives an alternative proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, for which a proof was previously presented in the OpenAI Math Release.

title: The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in real quadratic function fields
summary: Matomäki proved that if $α\in\R$ is irrational, then there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $|α-a/p|\le p^{-4/3+\varepsilon}$ for a suitable integer $a$. In \cite{BaMo}, Baier and the author established analogues of this result for $\F_q(T)$ and its imaginary quadratic extensions. In this paper, we extend it to all real quadratic extensions of $\F_q(T)$.

title: Near optimal gap in the Lonely Runner Conjecture
summary: For a set $V$ of $n$ distinct positive integers, let $\mathrm{ML}(V)=\max_{t\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\min_{v\in V}\|vt\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every $V$, \[ \mathrm{ML}(V)>\frac{1+c}{2n}. \] The proof combines a refinement of the large GCD argument of Green and Walker with a new physical spillover inequality for interval multiplicities.

title: A duality principle for the neighbourhood of manifolds and applications to counting rational points near curves
summary: In this paper, we establish a duality principle relating the count of rationals near a manifold to a sparse counting problem for the dual. As applications, we give a short, self-contained proof of sharp bounds for planar curves under minimal regularity conditions and similarly, sharp upper bounds for non- degenerate space curves, again under minimal curvature conditions. This work recovers and extends the works of Beresnevich, Dickinson and Velani and of Vaughan and Velani on planar curves and independently proves and extends the results of Chen, Seeger, Srivastava and Technau on space curves, while providing a structural picture well-suited for generalisations. The re- sults and methods of this work precede the emergence of highly capable AI models.

In this paper, first, following the original approach given by Kazhdan-Patterson and applying the block-compatible 2-cocycle of Banks-Levy-Sepanski, we fill in several details omitted in the original proof. Secondly, we compare the formula of Kazhdan-Patterson with that of McNamara and Gao, which is formulated in a more general setting.
